newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU maize exports to Slovenia at 25 Ecu refund - ONIC. [CORRECTED 21:23 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU maize exports to Slovenia at 25 Ecu refund - ONIC. [CORRECTED 21:23 GMT]

text.p: A dash or "nil value" entry will apply to all daily exports of European Union grain, excluding the export of up to 15,000 tonnes of maize to Slovenia, which will benefit from a refund of 25 Ecus per tonne, European Commission figures showed on Thursday.
(Corrects refund in headline and first paragraph from 15 Ecus per tonne and corrects attribution from French to European Commission figures.).
A refund of 30 Ecus per tonne continues to apply to daily rye flour exports, it said.

All monthly correctives for grain, excluding maize, are now at "nil value." Correctives for maize were set at zero for June, July, and August and a negative corrective of 25 Ecus per tonne will apply to maize exports in September and October.
The corrective for rye flour was set at zero for the June-October period.

On Thursday the European Union scrapped export taxes for all types of wheat and flour replacing them with a "nil value" entry, which means the licences are valid for just 30 days instead of the normal four to five months and their value cannot be fixed in advance.
